PHSCS 587

Constant-field scaling

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows how ideal constant-field scaling changes delay and switching energy

For a scale factor κ > 1, ideal constant-field scaling divides device dimensions and voltages by κ while multiplying doping by κ. With unchanged permittivity and mobility, electric field and carrier velocity remain unchanged.

Gate capacitance C scales as area/thickness, hence 1/κ. Current scales as 1/κ, and delay CV/I as 1/κ. Switching energy proportional to CV² scales as 1/κ³. At proportionally faster operation, per-device dynamic power scales as 1/κ² while ideal device density rises as κ², leaving power per area unchanged.

These are linked ideal assumptions, not a promise from shrinking lithography alone. Thermal voltage, bandgap and built-in potentials do not follow geometric scaling. Leakage, oxide tunneling, contact resistance and finite doping constrain the extrapolation.

Example

At κ = 2, the ideal model gives half the capacitance, current and delay, one eighth the switching energy and four times the device density. At twice the switching rate and unchanged activity, per-device dynamic power becomes one quarter.

Sources and scope
  • PHSCS 587 reading: 8.1–8.2.1.2, constant-field scaling

Practice

1. If dimensions shrink but voltage stays fixed, does the constant-field table still apply?

Track E ≈ V/length and the assumptions at the start of the derivation.

No. The field would rise, and the ideal linked voltage, current, delay and power scalings would no longer follow. A different scaling model is required.
